subsections.subsection_title: Sepsis, Severe Sepsis, qSOFA, Stages, SIRS and Septic Shock

blocks.text: Life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection.
Operationally: suspected/documented infection with an acute increase in SOFA score of ≥ 2 points.

items: Delayed capillary refill, mottled or cold extremities

blocks.text: Sepsis with organ dysfunction, hypoperfusion or sepsis-induced hypotension.
Under Sepsis-3, the term severe sepsis is redundant because sepsis already implies organ dysfunction.
Score ≥ 2: increased risk of poor outcome; urgent assessment for organ dysfunction.
qSOFA is not a diagnostic test and should not be used alone to screen out sepsis.

items: Sepsis with persistent circulatory/metabolic abnormalities requiring vasopressors to maintain MAP ≥ 65 mmHg and lactate > 2 mmol/L despite adequate fluid resuscitation.

blocks.text: Immediate actions — first hour when sepsis or septic shock is recognised
Measure serum lactate; repeat if elevated.
Obtain blood cultures before antibiotics if this does not delay treatment.
Administer broad-spectrum IV antibiotics promptly; immediately or within 1 hour for septic shock or high-likelihood sepsis.
Give IV crystalloid for hypotension or significant hypoperfusion; approximately 30 mL/kg within the first 3 hours is a common initial target, with frequent reassessment.
Start vasopressors if hypotension persists during/after fluid resuscitation; norepinephrine is first-line.
Aim for MAP ≥ 65 mmHg in most adults receiving vasopressors.
Identify and control the source: drainage, debridement, removal of infected devices or surgery when indicated.

subsections.subsection_title: Serum Albumin vs Ascitic Fluid and Calculations

blocks.text: Serum and ascitic albumin should be measured close together in time.

items: SAAG ≥ 1.1 g/dL (11 g/L): portal hypertension likely

blocks.text: High SAAG + protein ≥ 2.5 g/dL: commonly cardiac ascites or early Budd–Chiari syndrome
